Threat: Theft from vehicle during home visit
Vulnerability: No full-disk encryption on 15% of legacy fleet
Treatment Plan: Deploy full-disk encryption org-wide; complete by Q3; enforce via MDM

Vulnerability: Delayed patch cycle on EHR app servers
Treatment Plan: Move to enforced 72hr critical patch SLA with vendor; offline immutable backups

Threat: Phishing leading to EHR account compromise
Vulnerability: No MFA on legacy EHR mobile app version
Existing Controls: Password-only auth on older app version
Treatment Plan: Force upgrade to MFA-enabled app version; disable legacy auth endpoint

Threat: Data interception over unsecured home Wi-Fi
Vulnerability: Device firmware lacks TLS enforcement on some older units
Treatment Plan: Phase out unsupported device models; require gateway-side encryption for all new procurement
Automate deprovisioning via HR system trigger; target same-day revocation

Vulnerability: Some clinicians retain paper backups for connectivity gaps
Treatment Plan: Formalize physical PHI handling procedure; move toward offline-capable EHR app

Vulnerability: Platform lacks end-to-end encryption on free tier
Treatment Plan: Upgrade to enterprise tier with E2E encryption and BAA

Threat: Vendor breach exposing patient billing/PHI data
Vulnerability: Vendor has not provided current SOC 2 report
Treatment Plan: Require current SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 evidence annually; escalate if not provided

Threat: Malware on personal device used for work data
Vulnerability: No MDM enrollment on BYOD devices
Treatment Plan: Maintain strict app-level restriction preventing PHI on BYOD; annual policy re-attestation

Threat: Backup corruption undetected until needed during disaster
Treatment Plan: Implement quarterly mandatory restore test with sign-off
